about: Proposal by the 'caves' researcher, 2026-10-10. Nothing in the project was edited. Two cave targets whose scored climate values are MEASURED (orbital data at the site), so the 'shelter' resource and basalt lava caves such as Harrat al-Shaam count in the score. Values describe the ground surface around each skylight (the skylights are smaller than the map pixels); readings or models for the inside of the caves are facts only. To merge: add both 'targets' to data/targets.json, merge 'newSources' into its sources, add 'resources' to data/resources.json places, add 'terrainPoints' to data/terrain_points.json, add the 'moon-cave' and 'mars-cave' groups to the app (see appChangesNeeded), then run python -I scripts/compute_terrain.py --only tranquillitatis-pit --only arsia-skylight. Supersedes scratchpad/fix/pit_proposal.json for the Moon pit (its quotes and coordinates are reused). No ranking numbers here.

targets.name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit (cave skylight)
targets.mission: Proposed cave shelter for a Moon base (seen by LRO; no landing yet)

meanTemp.note: Surface temperature of the mare plain around the pit, not inside it (the Moon has no air): mean of the LRO Diviner day-night curve, 218.5 K, in the 0.5° (about 15 km) map bin that contains the pit (all nadir data 2009-2015, 15-minute local-time bins; 43 empty bins filled by straight lines between neighbours). The 100 m pit is far smaller than the bin. The eight bins around it give 217.8-222.3 K. Inside the shaded cave a model gives about 17 °C (see facts).

swing.note: Highest minus lowest point of the same Diviner day-night curve: 394.8 K near noon minus 93.8 K just before sunrise. Each point is the average of all observations in one 15-minute local-time bin. A lunar day lasts about 29.5 Earth days.

coldGround.note: Coldest point of the Diviner day-night curve in the bin with the pit: 93.8 K at about 05:20 local time, just before sunrise. It is a bin average, so single readings can be a little colder.

albedo.note: Not used: the only site value found is LOLA's laser normal albedo at 1064 nm (0.156, zero phase angle), a different quantity from the broadband surface albedo of the Earth sites (see facts).

facts.label: Map pin
facts.text: Mare Tranquillitatis pit, 8.3355° N, 33.222° E (LROC Lunar Pit Atlas); the temperatures above are for the flat mare plain around it

facts.label: Pit size
facts.text: Opening about 100 × 88 m inside a funnel about 146 × 140 m; 105 m deep below the funnel floor (the funnel is about 20 m deep). Measured from LRO camera stereo images

facts.label: Overhang
facts.text: The walls overhang by at least 10-15 m on the east, west and north sides; the open part of the floor is flat and covered in boulders

facts.label: Cave (radar)
facts.text: Part of the radar echoes from the pit come from a cave passage tens of metres long under the surface (LRO Mini-RF radar, 2010)

facts.label: Cave length
facts.text: More than 60 m (200 feet) from the base of the pit; the full length is unknown

facts.label: Night (measured)
facts.text: LRO Diviner sees the pit about 100 K warmer than the ground around it at night

facts.label: Night (measured, map)
facts.text: At midnight the 237 m Diviner map pixel that holds the pit reads 126.1 K, while the mare around it (1-6 km away) reads about 100.4 K: 26 K warmer, although the pit fills only part of the pixel

facts.label: Protection
facts.text: Pits or caves would also give some protection from cosmic rays, solar radiation and micrometeorites

facts.label: Geology
facts.text: Hard, dense basalt lava around the pit (judged from rocks and crater wear seen from orbit)

facts.label: Pit walls
facts.text: Pits in the lunar seas show the layers of the top 20-100 m of basalt lava flows

facts.label: Distance
facts.text: About 370 km (230 miles) north-east of the Apollo 11 landing site

facts.label: Air pressure
facts.text: about zero

facts.label: Hottest (surface)
facts.text: 394.8 K (+121.7 °C) near local noon, mare surface in the Diviner bin with the pit

facts.label: Night average (surface)
facts.text: 104 K (-169 °C) between 18:00 and 06:00 local time, same Diviner bin

facts.label: Inside the cave (model)
facts.text: A heat model checked against Diviner night data says the permanently shaded part under the overhang stays near 290 K (about 17 °C) all lunar day; this is a model result, not a reading

facts.label: Sunlit pit floor (model)
facts.text: Pit floors near the equator can reach more than 420 K (about 147 °C) at midday (model)

facts.label: Laser albedo (measured)
facts.text: LOLA normal albedo at 1064 nm: 0.156 in the 3 km map pixel with the pit (zero phase angle, one infrared wavelength; not the broadband albedo used for Earth sites)

targets.name: Arsia Mons cave skylight ('Jeanne')
targets.mission: Candidate cave entrance seen from orbit (Mars Odyssey THEMIS, MRO HiRISE); no landing yet

meanTemp.note: Average ground temperature from orbit (MRO Mars Climate Sounder, 25 km around the skylight). Seen near 3 AM and 3 PM only, so close to but not exactly a true average; ground, not air. It describes the dusty lava plain around the skylight, not the inside of the cave.

swing.note: Not measured: no measured daily range here. Orbit maps give only the warmest afternoon and coldest night over all seasons (warmest +3.9 °C).

coldGround.note: Coldest ground temperature seen by Mars Climate Sounder (144.5 K, 25 km mean, near 3 AM). The true pre-dawn minimum is probably a little colder.

albedo.note: MGS TES Lambert albedo, mean within 25 km of the skylight (not corrected for the atmosphere); a bright, dusty surface.

facts.label: Map pin
facts.text: Cave-entrance candidate APC075 ('Jeanne'), 5.5332° S, 241.3931° E (USGS Mars cave catalogue); the HiRISE image of it is centred at 5.532° S, 241.396° E

facts.label: Pit size
facts.text: About 165 m across and more than 245 m deep, with an overhanging rim of unknown extent (measured from orbital images and shadows)

facts.label: No floor seen
facts.text: HiRISE sees no detail in the shadow and cannot see the walls: they are vertical or, more likely, overhanging

facts.label: Evening (measured)
facts.text: In 4 THEMIS images taken about 18:15-19:15 local time (2017-2020), a spot within about 0.3 km of the skylight is 12-18 K warmer than the plain around it (166-181 K against 154-165 K; 100 m pixels)

facts.label: Afternoon (measured)
facts.text: At 14:46 local time (2009) the same spot is about 10 K cooler than the plain (263 K against 273 K); in 5 later-afternoon images the difference is 0-3 K

facts.label: Before dawn (measured)
facts.text: In 7 THEMIS images between 03:30 and 07:30 local time no clear difference shows at 100 m pixels

facts.label: Thermal behaviour (published)
facts.text: Floors of these deep pits are warmer at night and change much less between day and night than the ground around them (THEMIS)

facts.label: Warmest ground
facts.text: +3.9 °C (277.1 K), the warmest afternoon value in the Mars Climate Sounder maps (25 km mean, about 3 PM)

facts.label: Seven sisters
facts.text: One of seven candidate cave skylights found on the flanks of Arsia Mons with Mars Odyssey's THEMIS camera (reported 2007)

facts.label: Height
facts.text: About 10.0 km above the Mars datum (MOLA elevation at the pin)

facts.label: Landing
facts.text: The discoverers note that the air at these heights is too thin for a lander to slow down and steer onto such a small target

facts.label: Protection
facts.text: Lava-tube caves would shield people from dust storms, micrometeoroids and radiation, and keep temperatures steadier than the surface

facts.label: Surface
facts.text: A very dark hole in an otherwise bright, dusty lava plain north-east of Arsia Mons

facts.label: Lava flows
facts.text: Lava flows around Arsia Mons look very much like Hawaiian lava flows (THEMIS image of flows south of the volcano)

facts.label: Rock type
facts.text: Lava of a Tharsis shield volcano; NASA says such lava is most likely basalt. Inferred, not measured: dust hides the rock

geology.note: Inferred, not measured: shield-volcano lava under dust.

shelter.quote: This discovery suggests that the MTP is a promising site for a lunar base, as it offers shelter from the harsh surface environment and could support long-term human exploration of the Moon.
shelter.note: Carrer et al. 2024, Nature Astronomy (abstract). The same abstract: radar reflections 'can be attributed to a subsurface cave conduit tens of metres long'.

regolith.quote: We investigated the regolith parent rock (“protolith”) properties of Mare Tranquillitatis and Marius Hills on the Moon, utilizing lunar pit craters (“lua”) to contextualize observations of rock abundance and crater degradation.

notTagged.ice: No source for water ice at the pit was found.

shelter.quote: Seven possible skylight entrances into Martian caves were observed on and around the flanks of Arsia Mons by the Mars Odyssey Thermal Emission Imaging System (THEMIS).
shelter.note: Cushing et al. 2007, GRL (abstract, via OpenAlex). This pit is one of the seven ('Jeanne', MGC3 APC075). On why caves matter: 'Lava-tube caves, by their nature, can protect inhabitants from all of the hazards that humans would encounter on the surface.' (Cushing 2012, J. Cave Karst Stud., https://legacy.caves.org/pub/journal/PDF/V74/cave-74-01-33.pdf). A candidate only: the USGS catalogue says none can be verified as genuine caves from orbit.

regolith.quote: This image shows a very dark spot on an otherwise bright dusty lava plain to the northeast of Arsia Mons, one of the four giant Tharsis volcanoes.
regolith.note: HiRISE caption (A. McEwen, 2007). Weak tag: it shows loose dust on the surface at the site, not a measured regolith layer (compare Phoenix). Lead may drop it.

notTagged.ice: Cushing 2012 suggests caves near Arsia Mons could trap ice, but this is a hypothesis; no ice was detected here.

rule.text: A target needs at least 2 truly measured factors (rain = 0 counts). The app also flags (⚑) targets with fewer than 3 (TARGET_MIN_MEASURED in js/scoring.js).

measured: meanTemp -54.7 °C, swing 301.1 °C, coldGround -179.4 °C: LRO Diviner GCP day-night curve (bolometric brightness temperature, 2009-2015) in the 0.5° bin 8.0-8.5° N, 33.0-33.5° E that contains the pit; mare surface, not the pit

Midnight Diviner map (GHRM, 237 m pixels, 2009-2022): pit pixel 126.1 K vs 100.43 K median 1-5.7 km around (+25.7 K). The same pixel has the largest midnight anomaly (25.87 K) and Diviner rock abundance (0.1) in the 11.6 km window, which confirms the georeferencing
Night: pit about 100 K warmer than the surrounding surface (Diviner; horvath-2022 abstract)
LOLA 1064 nm normal albedo 0.1559 (3 km pixel) - measured, but not used as the scored albedo
Pit size and overhangs (LROC NAC images and stereo); radar echoes (Mini-RF); terrain (LOLA via Moon Trek); rain 0 (no atmosphere)
modelled_or_derived: About 290 K (~17 °C) in the permanently shaded cave part; >420 K on sunlit floors (horvath-2022 thermal model) -> facts only
Cave passage tens of metres long (fit of radar simulations, carrer-2024) -> fact and shelter tag
Basalt: inferred from orbital rock counts and crater wear (costello-2026)

GHRM midnight values come from an empirical fit of the measurements to exactly midnight; the GHRM 'anomaly' map is measurement minus a thermal model (cross-check only); rock abundance is a model fit (cross-check only)
meanTemp: 43 of 96 local-time bins are empty and filled by straight lines (mean of filled bins only: 218.53 K, almost the same)
notMeasured: any temperature reading inside the pit or cave

measured: meanTemp -72.3 °C and coldGround -128.7 °C: MRO MCS surface temperature maps, mean of 5 pixels within 25 km (project script data/raw/mars_ez_extract/mcs_extract.py; the same rule as the Deuteronilus and Erebus Montes targets)
albedo 0.28: MGS TES Lambert albedo, mean of 36 pixels within 25 km (project script data/raw/mars_ez_extract/tes_albedo.py)
THEMIS band-9 brightness temperatures at the skylight from 17 PDS images (evening warm spot +12 to +18 K; afternoon cool spot down to -10 K; nothing clear before dawn or in the morning) -> facts only
Position, size (~165 m) and minimum depth (>245 m) from orbital images and shadows (MGC3, HiRISE); terrain and height (MOLA via Mars Trek); rain 0
modelled_or_derived: MCS 'average' is the mean of ~3 AM and ~3 PM observations, close to but not exactly a true mean (dataset readme)
That it is a cave at all: inferred from orbit (no floor or walls visible); the USGS catalogue stresses none can be verified from orbit

gcp.rowOrderCheck: row = ilon*1920 + ilat*96 + ilt, checked by reading rows 0, 96, 1920 and the last row (clon/clat/ltim columns)

mcs.crossCheck: Same run gives Jezero avg 217.49 K, min 184.51 K, max 254.32 K, identical to data/raw/mars_ez_research.json

tes.crossCheck: Same run gives Deuteronilus 25 km mean 0.135 (targets.json: 0.14)

themis.method: PDS3 PBT label read for each image; pixel of the MGC3 point found in the SINUSOIDAL projection (conventions checked against each label's min/max latitude and west/east longitude); 25-line window read by HTTP Range. The evening warm spot and the 14:46 cool spot both sit 2 lines north and 2 samples west of the MGC3 pixel (about 0.28 km), so all images are summarised at that offset (3 x 3 pixels) against the median of pixels 6-12 px from the MGC3 point.

appChangesNeeded: js/ui/topbar.js TARGET_GROUPS has no 'moon-cave' (only a comment, contract C2) and no 'mars-cave'. Add {id:'moon-cave', label:'Moon · cave shelter (lava-tube pit)'} after 'moon-base' and e.g. {id:'mars-cave', label:'Mars · cave skylight (lava-flow pit)'} after 'mars-base'; otherwise the targets are not listed.
tests/index.html test 'every target is in a valid group, in the agreed order': ORDER and LABEL know 'moon-cave' but not 'mars-cave'. Add 'mars-cave' to both (after 'mars-base') or the test fails.
js/ui/tour.js GROUP_WORDS has 'moon-cave' but not 'mars-cave': add e.g. 'mars-cave': ['Mars cave skylight', 'Mars cave skylights'].
If the lead prefers no new Mars group, 'mars-base' is the closest existing group, but its label says 'proposed human landing zones (NASA, 2015)', which this site is not.
decisionsForLead: Moon pit: the scored values are now the MEASURED mare surface around the pit (Diviner), not the modelled 17 °C cave interior (which becomes a fact). This replaces the earlier proposal's meanTemp 17 / strict null and lifts the pit from 1 to 4 measured factors.

Both targets compare Earth air/ground climate with the ground surface outside the cave. The 'shelter' tag, basalt geology and terrain are what make them cave analogs; say so in the notes and in Method.

Moon albedo left null on purpose: LOLA 1064 nm zero-phase normal albedo (0.156) is measured but is a different quantity from NASA POWER broadband surface albedo; it is a fact. If the lead wants it scored, put 0.16 with that note (it would not change the pass/fail rule).
Mars regolith tag is weak (a 'dusty lava plain' caption). Keep or drop.
Mars name/ID: 'arsia-skylight' / "Arsia Mons cave skylight ('Jeanne')". 'Jeanne' is the discoverers' informal name (LPSC 2007); the USGS catalogue ID is APC075.
MGC3 table row lists depth 345 m while the MGC3 description and Cushing 2012 both say >245 m for this pit (HiRISE PSP_003647_1745); the proposal uses >245 m.

THEMIS facts are our own extraction from PDS images (the GRL 2007 full text with the authors' numbers is behind a Cloudflare check and was not read). If the lead wants only published numbers, keep the 'Thermal behaviour (published)' fact and drop the three THEMIS facts.
couldNotRead: Cushing et al. 2007 GRL and Cushing et al. 2015 JGR full texts: Wiley returns a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' check (not bypassed). Only abstracts (OpenAlex) are quoted; LPSC 2007 abstract 1371 (LPI) was read in full.
Horvath et al. 2022 full text (same Wiley check).
luna1.diviner.ucla.edu (UCLA Diviner level-4 site) timed out; the PDS copies of the same products were used instead.
Jung, Yi & Kim 2014 (JASS) PDF came back empty; it covers Pavonis/Ascraeus candidates anyway, not Arsia.

quotes.quote: NASA-funded scientists have discovered shaded locations within pits on the Moon that always hover around a comfortable 63 F (about 17 C) using data from NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) spacecraft and computer modeling.

quotes.quote: Focusing on a roughly cylindrical 328-foot (100-meter)–deep depression about the length and width of a football field in an area of the Moon known as the Mare Tranquillitatis, Horvath and his colleagues used computer modeling to analyze the thermal properties of the rock and lunar dust and to chart the pit’s temperatures over time.

quotes.quote: The results revealed that temperatures within the permanently shadowed reaches of the pit fluctuate only slightly throughout the lunar day, remaining at around 63 F or 17 C.

quotes.quote: The pits, and caves to which they may lead, would make thermally stable sites for lunar exploration compared to areas at the Moon’s surface, which heat up to 260 F (about 127 C) during the day and cool to minus 280 F (about minus 173 C) at night.
